newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tight security at HK hotel where China leaders to stay.
newsitem.headline: Tight security at HK hotel where China leaders to stay.

text.p: Security was tight on Sunday at the hotel where China's leaders are expected to stay during Britain's handover of Hong Kong to China.

President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen will lead the Chinese delegation in the ceremony at midnight on Monday to mark the return of Hong Kong to China after 156 years of colonial rule.
More than two dozen uniformed police officers guarded the Harbour Plaza View hotel at the waterfront in Hung Hom, a residental district on the Kowloon peninsula.
They barred taxis and other vehicles from going in to the hotel, which is owned by tycoon Li Ka-shing, one of Beijing's trusted confidants.

Police cleared onlookers from the pavement across from the hotel. Guests and visitors were subjected to checks before they could enter. They had to go through metal detectors, while bags and luggage were X-rayed.
A red carpet was rolled out and the grand staircase in the middle of the lobby was draped with red-and-gold ribbon.
Marine police in combat fatigues were guarding the pier outside where two police speedboats, usually deployed for anti-smuggling activities, were docked.
